PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE INCORPORATORS

The undersigned shareholders of the proposed French SARL hereby adopt the following:

RESOLVED that the Company shall have a minimum share capital of 1 Euro (1 EUR), subscribed in full by the incorporators as detailed below: [Shareholder 1] 50% and [Shareholder 2] 50%.

RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be established at the address [Full Address], France, and all corporate documents shall be maintained there.

RESOLVED that the following persons are appointed as corporate officers with full management powers: [Name] as Président, [Name] as gérant, and [Name] as commissaire aux comptes.

RESOLVED that the Articles of Association be adopted in the form provided, and that the Président be authorized to submit the acte de constitution to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for registration, complete any necessary formalities, and represent the Company in all dealings.

This resolution is passed unanimously on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the complete statuts de la SARL including company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, management structure, and signatures of all shareholders. Ensure compliance with French legal requirements.
required_dossiers: Shareholder IDs and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe queries the filing, provide clarifications or file amended documents within the specified period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the signed draft statuts to a notary for authentication. The notary verifies the signatures and legal capacity of the shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notary will advise on any required modifications; corrections can be made before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via online portal or in person
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated acte de constitution and statuts to the greffe. The greffe will register the company, assign SIREN/SIRET numbers, and issue the certificate of incorporation. Pay any nominal fees if applicable.
required_dossiers: Proof of capital subscription and payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant must provide additional documents or information within the deadline or request a hearing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspections by certified professionals; workplace safety clearance from the Labour Inspectorate

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr; corporate and VAT formalities filed through the National Business Formalities Portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); customs clearance administered by Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via Pro.Douane DELTA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity engaged in taxable supplies in France must register for French corporate income tax (Société à Responsabilité Limitée subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés) and VAT by filing the standard incorporation/formalities dossier unless it only requires VAT identification. Non-EU entities must appoint an accredited tax representative in France in accordance with CGI Article 289-A. The local SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) allocates the SIREN/SIRET numbers and the intra-Community French VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire), which is also required for customs declarations and electronic invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in France. A small SARL meeting the statutory conditions may elect fiscal transparency under CGI Article 239 bis AA, thereby being taxed under the income tax (IR) partnership regime rather than corporate income tax. A qualifying SARL may also elect for group fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under CGI Article 223-A. Hybrid mismatch elections are restricted by ATAD/anti-hybrid provisions codified in CGI Articles 202 quater and 205 and by administrative doctrine; aggressive hybrid-electivity is disallowed.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Foreign entities have no de minimis VAT registration threshold: any taxable supply of goods or services physically performed in France, including temperature-controlled warehousing, triggers immediate French VAT registration. Domestic micro-businesses may invoke the franchise en base de TVA (€91,900 for goods / €36,800 for services annual turnover), but this relief is practically irrelevant for cold-chain B2B warehousing contracts and is not available to non-established suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates progressive B2B electronic invoicing under the anticompliance reform: all companies must be able to receive structured e-invoices from September 1, 2026, with issuance obligations phased to large/mid-size undertakings from September 2026 and extended to SMEs/micro-businesses from September 2027. Invoices must be transmitted through certified Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs) or the public portal Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) in national structured formats (Factur-X 1.0.07 / CII / UBL 2.1) under the Y-model, whereby transactional and e-reporting data flow to DGFiP without real-time fiscal stamping. Authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and readability are compulsory; electronic signatures or secure EDI exchanges are accepted evidencing audit trails.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under CGI Article 262-I to goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union, provided the customs export declaration is accepted by DGDDI and definitive proof of exit from EU territory is held. Temperature-controlled storage and related handling services may qualify for exemption under CGI Article 262-II-2° where the service is directly and exclusively connected to a completed export of the goods, even if performed in a French customs warehouse or free zone. Services performed for goods remaining in France or moving intra-EU are not zero-rated; absent the direct-export link, warehousing is localized where the goods are physically located and attracts French VAT at 20%, subject to B2B place-of-supply reverse-charge rules only where the statutory localization rules so provide.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU) electronically lodged via DELTA/DDN with DGDDI and accepted for export
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport instrument evidencing physical departure of goods from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export stock release order cross-referencing the DAU reference
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MF payment credit evidence matching the export invoice value and confirming the foreign buyer's payment
Bonded warehouse or free-zone inventory movement records, storage tickets, and customs warehouse permits evidencing the physical presence and exit of the exact goods
Delivery acceptance certificate or destination customs clearance proof issued by the importing country (where obtainable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may reopen and reassess VAT periods for the standard 3-year reprise window, extended to 10 years where the activity was concealed or fraudulent documentation is established; unsupported export zero-rating entries are clawed back in full with per-month late payment interest (intérêts de retard, currently 0.20% per month). Penalties escalate as follows: 40% for deliberate inaccuracies under CGI Article 1729-a; 80% for fraudulent maneuvers, abuse of right, or use of fabricated export documents under CGI Article 1729-b; specific fines up to €1,500 for failure to produce required documentation. Criminal prosecution under CGI Article 1741 for export VAT fraud may result in imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to €75,000, increased to €150,000 in aggravated circumstances, alongside permanent disqualification of the managing director.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the competent national authority for foreign-exchange oversight, balance-of-payments statistics and the administration of economic transaction declarations under the Code monétaire et financier; prudential supervision of banks and payment institutions is exercised jointly by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the French supervisory authority and the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Single Supervisory Mechanism; the eurozone clearing infrastructure (TARGET2, T2S, and SEPA clearing) is operated through the Eurosystem with French books settled via Banque de France systems.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France offers full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no foreign-exchange controls, no prior administrative authorisation for inbound capital injections, no quantitative limits on outbound profit remittances, and no restriction on the currency denomination of payments. Practical hurdles for profit remittances by the SARL are limited to: (i) French corporate-law distribution rules (Code de commerce Articles L232-10 to L232-12) requiring the statutory legal reserve of 5% of annual net profit up to 10% of share capital to be withheld and prohibiting distributions when net equity is reduced below half of corporate capital; (ii) the 25% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders, which may be reduced to 0% where the recipient parent satisfies the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive holding requirements (at least 10% interest, two-year holding) or a double-tax-treaty rate otherwise applies; and (iii) for individual non-resident shareholders, the flat prélèvement forfaitaire unique of 12.8% plus social levies, with repatriation subject to treaty allocation. All foreign-exchange transactions with third-country residents must be reported to the Banque de France for statistical and balance-of-payments purposes when they exceed the regulatory de minimis threshold, and direct investment flows are covered by the mandatory direct-investment declaration regime. No exchange-rate gain or loss can be classified as non-resident or blocked.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation exists in France. A French entity conducting refrigerated logistics (ISIC 5210 / NAICS 493120) is not required to convert, repatriate, or surrender export proceeds or payments for services rendered to non-residents; there is no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export invoices may be denominated in EUR or any freely convertible currency and may be credited to foreign-currency accounts held at any euro-area bank, or paid through SWIFT to foreign accounts, without central-bank authorisation. The sole remaining obligation is the Banque de France statistical declaration of payments received from non-residents above the applicable reporting threshold under the balance-of-payments instructions, together with the standard VAT and customs reporting (intra-EU reverse-charge reporting under Article 283-1 of the Code général des impôts; EU customs monthly declarations for goods movements).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Blocking Escrow Account (Compte de Dépôt Bloqué) for incorporation funds; primary operational current account (Compte Courant Professionnel) with multi-currency capability, SWIFT GPI, and trade-finance desk for documentary credits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. (regional Caisse Régionale de Crédit Agricole Mutuel)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte de Dépôt) with SEPA/IBAN rails, intra-group sweep lines, invoice financing, and asset-based lending available for temperature-controlled warehouse equipment.

Operational Account (Compte Courant) together with statutory share-capital escrow sub-account (Compte Séquestre); dedicated international cash-management and confirming desk for pharmaceutical cold-chain clients.
Multi-currency professional account package with seasonal working-capital facilities and payment-aggregation services for logistics fee collections.
Standard corporate operational account with SEPA direct debit/credit clearing and local corporate treasury services; limited off-EUR FX appetite.
Generic operational account under public-law corporate vehicle; acceptable only as a secondary collection account due to limited FX and trade-finance product range.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rated Medium-to-High for ancillary treasury uses but strictly Inadmissible as the principal or sole banking relationship. An EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) passporting into France under PSD2 (e.g., a fintech with an ACPR or EEA-home-state authorisation) is feasible as a collection and disbursement rail for low-risk, non-deposit operations: receiving EUR/non-EUR revenue from pharmaceutical logistics clients, issuing local IBANs for client wire settlement, and executing outbound SWIFT MT103 payments. However, an EMI is not a credit institution under French banking law, and therefore cannot (i) hold the statutory capital-blocked escrow deposit required for SARL formation, (ii) grant overdrafts, credit lines, or factoring, or (iii) provide documentary letters of credit or FX hedging under banking safe-harbour rules. Given the target payment rails (ACH/Direct and Bank Wire) and the highly regulated perishing-pharmaceutical storage scope, the treasury blueprint mandates a tier-1 ACPR-regulated bank as the master treasury account holder, with at most one licensed EMI used as a segregated receivable-collection sub-rail holding less than 5% of aggregate treasury float, with full UBO passporting documentation and agreements in French governed by the Code monétaire et financier.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Articles L561-5 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier and ACPR Position 2016-01, the account-opening bank must positively identify the legal representative, every signatory, and the ultimate beneficial owner, using either physical presence or an eIDAS-recognised remote electronic identification process of equivalent assurance. In practice, for a newly formed SARL with non-EU resident shareholder-managers, French tier-1 banks universally require at least one in-person appearance of the gérant or a formally mandated representative holding a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, accompanied by original identity documents, the Kbis extract, the Articles of Association, and the UBO register declaration. A fully remote opening is generally tolerated only where the gérant holds a second principal residence in France, the use of a video-verification tool certified by the ACPR is deployed, or the existing group relationship manager sponsors the validation; the safest pathway is a first physical banking interview in Paris or Lyon, followed by remote standard operation. All onboarding interviews are recorded in the obligatory compliance record and retained for five years after account closure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly registered SARL (less than three months old) with no historical financial statements, requesting immediate opening and high-volume wire facility before first commercial activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the RCS tax-identification Kbis extract issued within 90 days, the signed Articles of Association and proof of legal-form filing, the bank-issued capital blocking certificate, the registered warehouse lease (bail commercial) with at least a 36-month term, the prefecture/ministry licence for temperature-controlled storage (ISIC 5210), a 12-month liquidity and P&L forecast, the ISO 13485 / EU GDP (Good Distribution Practice) certificate covering pharmaceutical cold-chain warehousing, and the complete UBO declaration certified with natural-person identity documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a third-country direct shareholder executed in USD or routed through an intermediary financial institution, triggering elevation to enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarised and apostilled share-subscription or contribution agreement with French translation, audited six-month statements of the direct shareholder evidencing lawful source of funds, the tax-residence certificate from the shareholder's competent authority, a group organisational chart, the minutes of the extraordinary general meeting resolving the capital increase, and contemporaneous FX trade confirmations from two independent regulated banks to demonstrate value-chain coherence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity due to a tiered international holding chain (e.g., Luxembourg or Delaware intermediate holding with nominee directors).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File and provide the formal UBO declaration with the INPI registry including the declaration receipt, a chain-of-ownership diagram with percentages and control indicators certified by a public accountant, passport copies of each ultimate beneficial owner, authorisation resolutions of the intermediate holding board, and the beneficial owner's undertaking to maintain updated filings every filing cycle, coupled with a negative media/sanctions screening report from a commercial due-diligence database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reference to pharmaceutical or medical-logistics counterparties in OECD/EU sanctions-high-risk jurisdictions triggering trade-based money-laundering scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the bank-end EU/OFAC sanctions-screening reports with no-hit status, the DGEFP (Direction générale des entreprises et de la propriété industrielle) import/export licences where dual-use goods are indicated, the precise customs codes, the customer due-diligence file of the counterparty, the full distribution contract with governing law and place-of-payment clauses, and the compulsorily retained temperature-monitoring records linking physical storage to the invoiced service, with all shipments routed through reputable approved correspondents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency outbound wires to freight forwarders, subcontracted cold-chain carriers, and utility suppliers which may be flagged as phantom-transaction patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble and retain a transaction-aligned logistics line: WMS inbound/outbound records, CMR/CIM consignment notes with signed delivery proof and geolocation truck-logs, temperature-logger PDF records, VAT reverse-charge documentation for intra-EU B2B services, reconciliation schedules pairing each wire to invoice numbers, and the underlying framework transport and warehousing contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The SARL's injection protocol uses a dedicated statutory escrow sub-account at a licensed French credit institution for the incorporation phase (blocked funds), followed by release to the operational current account after RCS registration. EUR-denominated injections from EEA shareholders are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer with the ISO 20022 reference field carrying the exact corporate purpose code 'EQUI' (equity contribution) or 'ADVA' (shareholder advance 'compte courant d'associé'); third-country contributions and amounts above materiality use SWIFT MT103 (SWIFT GPI) with the same purpose-code discipline and the beneficiary IBAN of the blocked sub-account, remitter bank details, and the SARL's RCS registration reference. The bank issues an 'attestation de dépôt des fonds' (capital-blocking certificate) only after full receipt and value-in; funds are then released against the RCS registration certificate (Kbis) and the correctly filed Articles of Association. For USD/GBP contributions, a standing spot-conversion mandate or an outright forward purchase of EUR hedges the conversion at the receiving bank; all capital movements exceeding the Banque de France reporting threshold are declared on the direct-investment form and the underlying purpose-code evidence is retained for anti-money-laundering inspection for at least five years. No inward wire may be credited to the operational account without passing the sanctions-maintenance and beneficiary-consistency screen at the compliance level.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic and euro-area payables (freight, energy, salaries, warehouse utilities, maintenance of refrigeration units) are settled via SEPA Instant Credit or SEPA Credit Transfer with a complete Unstructured Remittance Identifier linking invoice number and warehouse reference. Non-EEA trade settlements (refrigerated trailer equipment, IT software, international suppliers, customs broking fees) are routed through SWIFT MT103 using European balance-of-payments purpose labels (e.g., codes for goods purchase '101' or general services 'commercial services') and screened against SWIFT sanctions lists. For capital expenditure above EUR 25,000 and for pharmaceutical inbound cargo adjudication, an irrevocable documentary commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) opened by the French bank with the supplier as beneficiary is admitted, with transport documents, CMR, customs entry, and signed proof-of-delivery forming the presentation set; a confirmed L/C by a top-tier European bank is added in case of third-country suppliers with a sovereign or bank risk. All outbound disbursements must match the tax/VAT filing records; intra-group management-fee flows are executed by SEPA CT supported by an invoice and transfer-pricing documentation summary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) for committed commercial receivables and payables with tenors up to 12 months
FX swap (spot against forward, or forward-forward) for managing temporary currency liquidity mismatches and rolling over commercial positions
Cross-currency swap (EUR vs USD) matched to an underlying multi-year capital or shareholder-financing obligation
Vanilla OTC European FX option (purchase of call or put) with a licensed ACPR/EBA credit counterparty, without leverage, for hedging uncertain cold-storage capacity sales

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) strictly limited to restricted-convertibility or offshore-currency exposures (e.g., CNY, INR, TRY) where no deliverable onshore market lawfully exists; NDFs are not used for liquid G10 pairs
Natural hedge and netting agreements with group treasury for recurring multi-currency flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (annual accounts filing) with rapport de gestion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique / INPI RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the fiscal year-end: shareholder approval meeting must be held within 6 months of year-end and filed within 1 month of approval, but not later than the 7th month after closing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers formal notice, 2-month injunction period, court-imposed penalties (up to €3,000 or daily penalty), and eventual administrative strike-off ('radiation') from the RCS for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI / RCS through the Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due at the same time as the annual accounts filing; annual confirmation must be filed no later than the statutory accounts deposit deadline (generally within 7 months after fiscal year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers enforceable notice, potential court-ordered injunction, fine up to €15,000, and temporary blocking of extracts of Kbis certificates, escalating to RCS strike-off for persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Liasse fiscale (corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers: second business day after 3 May (typically 4-5 May). For a non-calendar fiscal year: within 3 months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 10% surcharge on tax due plus 0.4% per month late-payment interest; after formal notice, automatic penalties increase to 20%, and deliberate non-compliance can trigger 50% surcharge.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for SARLs exceeding at least two of the following three thresholds at the close of the second consecutive fiscal year: total assets > €4,000,000, annual net turnover > €8,000,000, average workforce > 50 employees. Audit also becomes mandatory if a member owning ≥10% of capital requests it via court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général - PCG), compliant with the French Commercial Code; IFRS is required only for consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every French RCS-registered entity must maintain a register of beneficial owners at the registered office and file an annual UBO declaration with INPI. The confirmation must be submitted at the same time as the annual accounts, and any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days from the date of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500-$1,500 per year (Paris-region registered office or professional agent fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000-$12,000 per year (depending on turnover, assets, and filing group)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate under Article 219 of the French General Tax Code (CGI). A reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 38,120 of annual taxable profit for SMEs whose turnover does not exceed EUR 10,000,000 and whose share capital is fully paid up and held at least 75% by individuals.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays exist in France. Applicable preferential provisions for a cold-storage logistics SARL include: reduced 15% CIT rate on the first earnings tranche; Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (CIR) for qualifying R&D in cold-chain or pharma stability engineering; Crédit d'Impôt Innovation (CII) for prototype and innovation pilot expenditure; Crédit d'Impôt pour l'Industrie Verte (CIV) for investments reducing environmental impact; and accelerated depreciation for energy-efficiency or refrigeration equipment under Article 39 AB CGI. The Jeune Entreprise Innovante (JEI) full exemption is normally unavailable to pure logistics operators.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: unlimited — carried-forward tax losses are deductible from future French taxable profits indefinitely. For losses generated in financial years ended on or before 31 December 2023, the annual deduction is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding that threshold. Losses arising in fiscal years closing from 31 December 2024 are not subject to that annual cap unless anti-abuse rules apply. A tax-loss carry-back is available for one year, limited to EUR 1,000,000, under Article 220 quinquies CGI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (annual corporate income tax return and financial statements) together with supporting schedules in the 2050-series (balance sheet, income statement, provisions, and tax credits). Electronically filed through the EFI/EDI professional web service on impots.gouv.fr or via the government-certified e-filing interfaces.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with four mandatory quarterly instalment payments (acomptes) using Form 2571-SD, and one final balance payment (solde) with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending 31 December, the annual return must be filed by the second working day after 1 May of the following year. For off-calendar fiscal years, the return is due no later than the end of the third month after the closing of the fiscal year, or one month following the expiry of the statutory information period where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 — Bénéfice net fiscal avant imputation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (profit) for the fiscal year before deducting carried-forward losses and applying tax credits. Includes turnover from refrigerated warehousing, handling fees, temperature-monitoring service fees, and any re-billed utilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder company operating through a French permanent establishment (PE) must report only the French-source PE profit. If the SARL is itself a French tax-resident entity with non-resident legal ownership, this box captures the entity's worldwide income as taxed in France; treaty PE attribution rules apply where the management decision-making is located abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory net tax loss for the current fiscal year, to be used for carry-forward or carry-back where eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must ensure the loss is computed solely against the French PE's accounts and in accordance with the authorised OECD approach (AOA). Losses incurred outside the French PE scope cannot be offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3519 / Schedule 2058-B — Report des déficits antérieurs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of prior-year loss carry-forward deductions applied to current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses of the French PE that arose while the entity was within the French tax net may be carried forward. For a non-resident parent, a change in treaty PE status between years can sever loss continuity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 330 / Schedule 2058-N — Crédits d'impôt et réductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate input of tax credits and reductions, including research credit, innovation credit, apprenticeship tax credit, or energy transition credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities are generally not eligible for offsettable French CIR/CII refunds unless they have a French PE or are residents of a DTA-eligible state that grants such refunds; attach the relevant proof of entitlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or late filing triggers a 10% surcharge under Article 1728 CGI, increased to 20% if the return is not filed within 30 days of a formal notice, 40% where the omission is committed intentionally, and 80% where fraud or use of a sham arrangement is proven. Late payment interest accrues at 0.30% per month. Additional penalties under Article 1743 may be imposed for knowingly omitting a substantial portion of turnover, jointly with the criminal offence of fraud.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD (quarterly corporate income tax instalment voucher) filed and settled online via the professional EFI portal on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly, due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December of each fiscal year, followed by the final balance due with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are payable on fixed calendar dates. The final balance payment is due on the same deadline as the annual return (second working day after 1 May for calendar-year taxpayers).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARL legal form, SIREN/SIRET, registered office, share capital, and tax identification details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the legal address of the French registered office; a management à l'étranger must nevertheless list a representative fiscal agent in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of the quarterly instalment calculated at 25% of the estimated annual CIT, reduced by credits and carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the estimated taxable profit of the French PE; if no PE is yet recognised by the tax administration, file on a precautionary basis to avoid late payment penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate eligibility for the small-business reduced rate or a specific tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent companies controlling the French SARL must verify that the reduced 15% rate still qualifies under the majority-shareholding condition.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment or underpayment of the required quarterly instalment gives rise to a 5% increase on the unpaid amount under Article 1730 CGI, plus 0.30% monthly interest. If the final balance is not paid by the filing deadline, the same surcharge and interest accrue automatically.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Article 187 of the French General Tax Code for dividend distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders outside the EU/EEA; 12.8% withholding plus 17.2% social levies (total 30% flat tax) apply to dividends paid to non-resident individuals. No French withholding tax applies to EU/EEA parent companies holding at least 10% of the SARL's capital for at least two years under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must request an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its own tax authority and submit it, together with the completed French withholding-tax relief form (the attestation de résidence fiscale, Form 5002/5003 as appropriate), to the French Tax Office (SIH) before the distribution date. For EU/EEA parent companies, the SARL must retain a signed holding declaration (attestation de détention) confirming the 10% stake and two-year holding condition. Relief at source can be granted only when the documentation is complete and anti-abuse screening is satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for patents, trademarks, software, know-how or industrial know-how paid to non-residents are subject to French withholding tax at the statutory rate of 33.33% under Article 182 B bis CGI. Under most tax treaties this is reduced, typically to 0% or 5% for commercial royalties, and 10% for copyright royalties. Interest: statutory French withholding tax is 0% where the beneficial owner is resident in a country having an administrative-assistance agreement, and 75% for payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions. Under standard French treaties interest is usually taxed at 0% if real benefit is held by a resident of the contracting state.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 — a French SARL is required to prepare and file the Local File when its gross annual turnover or total assets exceed EUR 400,000,000, or when the group to which it belongs has consolidated turnover/total assets above that threshold and the French entity is a significant participant. The Country-by-Country Report obligation arises when the consolidated group turnover is at least EUR 750,000,000. Even below those thresholds, all related-party cross-border transactions must satisfy the arm's-length principle and contemporaneous documentation must be retained upon tax audit request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply the Gulf-regime Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as a standalone statute. However, substantive presence is required through the French anti-abuse doctrine (abus de droit) under Article L.64 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales, the OECD BEPS PE attribution rules, and the EU ATAD general anti-abuse rule. A cold-storage SARL must maintain genuine premises in France, employed personnel, functioning refrigeration and monitoring equipment, local management decisions, and real exposure to operational risk. Absent economic substance, the tax administration may recharacterise the SARL as a sham, disregard its legal form, and tax its income at the level of the foreign owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully under-declaring warehousing turnover, issuing fictitious invoices for storage capacity, recording bogus temperature-controlled inventory, or concealing receipts from pharmaceutical clients in offshore accounts. Also includes using a formally valid SARL without any real cold-chain activity to escape French taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI, aggravated tax evasion is punishable by up to 7 years' imprisonment and a criminal fine of EUR 1,000,000, increaseable to twice the sum evaded. Companies face a corporate fine multiplied by five under Article 131-38 of the Criminal Code. The Tax Administration may simultaneously impose a 40% penalty for bad faith or 80% for organised sham arrangements, plus 0.30% monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant (and, where applicable, the president) can be sentenced to imprisonment and personally fined. French case law allows the fiscal authority to seek joint and several civil liability (action en insuffisance d'actif) against directors who caused or aggravated a deficiency in corporate assets. Travel bans (interdiction de quitter le territoire), asset freezing, and professional disqualification for up to 10 years are common ancillary orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / artificial arrangement / abus de droit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an empty SARL with a rented correspondence address and no actual cold-storage personnel, no physical temperature-monitoring facility, and no real commercial substance solely to claim French tax residence, benefit from a tax treaty, or access EU directives. Also includes artificially splitting one business into multiple SARLs to multiply exempt thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Tax Administration may recharacterise the arrangement under Article L.64 LPF and assess corporate income tax, social contributions and VAT in the hands of the true economic owner. The monetary penalty is 80% of the reassessed amount for abusive arrangements with an artificial purpose, or 40% without that intent, plus late payment interest. Criminal courts may also apply a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be treated as the actual taxable persons (la personne réellement bénéficiaire) and held personally liable for the 80% penalty. Courts may pierce the corporate veil based on fictive company evidence, leaving the gérant jointly liable for all corporate tax debts. Directors may be barred from managing any company in France for up to 15 years and subjected to a travel ban while criminal proceedings are active.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money-Laundering (AML) / failure to report to Tracfin
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cold-storage and pharmaceutical logistics services used to mask the origin of diverted medicines, counterfeit products, or unlawful proceeds; failure to perform basic KYC due diligence on commercial clients; accepting cash payments above statutory thresholds; or deliberately omitting transaction records for suspicious pharmaceutical supply chains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Article 324-1 of the French Criminal Code attracts 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 375,000. Aggravated laundering (habitual, organised, or using professional activity) carries 10 years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 fine. Company-level AML compliance failures under the Code monétaire et financier are subject to administrative sanctions of up to EUR 5,000,000 for non-credit institutions or, when AGEC is involved, fines matching 10% of turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A gérant who knowingly participates in laundering can be convicted as the principal offender, resulting in imprisonment, a substantial fine, and civil liability for repatriating laundered assets. The court may order confiscation of personal assets, travel bans, and prohibition of any professional activity during or after the sentence. Directors are held to the managerial AML duty; failure to establish and enforce a compliance programme gives rise to personal administrative sanctions by Tracfin and the competent supervisory body.
